title: As on a mountain
hookLine: live as if on a mountain; here or there matters little (Meditations 10.15)

cards: People dream of the cabin. The mountain view, the quiet, the place where you'll finally be the calm, wise version of yourself.
Back in book four, Marcus noted that people seek retreats in the country, by the sea, in the hills, and said you can retreat into yourself instead.
In book ten he comes at the same idea from the other side, with a short, strong instruction.

teach.h: LIFE IS SHORT; LIVE AS ON A MOUNTAIN.
teach.b: Here it is, in George Long's 1862 translation: “Short is the little which remains to thee of life. Live as on a mountain.”
It makes no difference, Marcus goes on, whether a person lives here or there, as long as they live everywhere in the world as a citizen of one great city. The mountain isn't a place you move to.
It's a way of standing: above the noise, seeing far, not tangled in every small quarrel of the town below. Let people see, he says, let them know, a real human being living by nature.
And then a hard line: if they can't stand him, let them kill him, because that's better than living the way they live.

It's the voice of a man who knew public life could be dangerous, and who wanted to be the same in public as in private. So why the mountain and not the cabin? The cabin promises you'll be different somewhere else.
Marcus says the shortness of life means there's no time to wait for the right setting.
The height has to come with you, into the office, the kitchen, the commute.
Here or there matters little. What you carry matters a great deal.

how: Readers of Marcus often use the mountain as a mental vantage point: in the middle of daily friction they picture the wide view, and try to act as they would from there.

games.q: you're Marcus, stuck in the noise of the court, and you long for a quiet place. what does book ten tell you?
o: live here as on a mountain; here or there matters little.
wait for retirement to start living well.
games.why: it makes no difference whether you live here or there, he writes, if you live everywhere in the world as a citizen.

practice: If you can, sit somewhere high or quiet, a top step, a window, a balcony, a hill, or a corner where the noise drops; otherwise, picture a mountain ledge.
From up there, look down at today's small tangles, the email, the argument, the errand, and see how small and far away they look. Then remember that you'll carry this view back down with you.

wordCard.voice: George Long, whose translation gives Marcus's instruction: short is the little that remains of life, so live as on a mountain. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a mountain. Marcus asks himself to live as on one.

carryVoice: Your line: here or there matters little. The height comes with you. See you tomorrow.
